title: Black Seeded Simpson Lettuce: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Black Seeded Simpson Lettuce: Yield and Maturity
metaDescription: Black Seeded Simpson lettuce is a leaf lettuce variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Black Seeded Simpson lettuce is a leaf lettuce variety, also sold or known as Black Simpson lettuce or Lettuce Leafy Blk. Simpson. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1970. B.M. Domingo bred it. It takes 33 to 40 days from sowing to harvest.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Black Simpson lettuce or Lettuce Leafy Blk. Simpson, this is the same lettuce. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [lettuce variety finder](/crop-varieties/lettuce), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Black Seeded Simpson lettuce takes 33 to 40 days from sowing to harvest. That is 22.2 days faster than the average of the 5 lettuce varieties with a day count, 58.7 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more. Its seller gives 33 to 40 days in the Seed Board record, Ramgo's packet says 45 to 50 days after transplanting.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit lettuce fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [damping off](/diseases/damping-off), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Leaves: loose leaf type, no head.
**Where:** Lowland to highland (the Seed Board rates it for both low and high elevation).

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of the five lettuces on the old Philippine Seed Board list and still sold as a Ramgo garden packet. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Black Seeded Simpson lettuce

Loose leaf lettuce grows in the lowlands, while heading types need the highlands. Pick a variety slow to bolt in the heat. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: Is Black Simpson lettuce the same as Black Seeded Simpson?
items.a: Yes. Black Simpson lettuce is another name for Black Seeded Simpson. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 33 to 40 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Black Seeded Simpson?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
